extracted.intended_audience: General readers, Tumblr users, researchers, and observers of platform features and content-moderation policy
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive overview of Tumblr's product features, posting rules, content-moderation policies, legal settlements, and operational constraints that govern how users post, tag, monetize, and appeal content on the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagging system limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first 20 tags added to any post will be indexed by the site. The tags are prefaced by a hashtag and separated by commas, and spaces and special characters are allowed, but only up to 140 characters total per tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use descriptive tags (e.g. #art, #sky) to make posts discoverable; be aware only the first 20 tags are indexed. Tags can also be used as commentary/meta-commentary (unique Tumblr convention) instead of altering the post content, but not all users prefer this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post types and dashboard actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The dashboard allows the user to upload text posts, images, videos, quotes, or links to their blog and to comment, reblog, and like posts from other blogs that appear on their dashboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dashboard is the primary interaction surface; users can also connect posts to Twitter and Facebook so posts are cross-posted. As of June 2022, users can turn off reblogs on specific posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Queue scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Users are able to set up a schedule to delay posts they make; they can spread their posts over several hours or even days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Queue to plan and pace content rather than posting all at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: HTML theme editing and custom themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr allows users to edit their blog's theme using HTML to control the appearance of their blog. Custom themes are able to be shared and used by other users, or sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTML editing provides full control over blog appearance; theme creators can monetize by selling themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom domains policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr allows users to use custom domains for their blogs, but users must purchase a domain from Tumblr Domains (an in-house registrar) that provides domains usable only with Tumblr unless removed. Legacy custom domains registered outside Tumblr remain functional if they are not disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New external domain linking was restricted after Tumblr Domains introduction; legacy users retained existing external domains as long as they remain connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe Mode and sensitive-content filtering (default opt-out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe Mode (which filters 'sensitive' content and blogs) became enabled by default for all users on an opt-out basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe Mode filters content from searches and tagged displays for logged-out or opt-in users. The system combines algorithmic detection and manual review; users reported many false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: December 2018 adult-content ban (scope and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective December 17, 2018, Tumblr banned all images and videos depicting sex acts, and real-life images and videos depicting human genitalia or 'female-presenting' nipples. Exceptions: illustrations or art that depict nudity, nudity related to 'political or newsworthy speech', and depictions of 'female-presenting' nipples in relation to medical events such as childbirth, breastfeeding, mastectomy and gender reassignment surgery. The rules do not apply to text content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All posts violating the policy are hidden from public view; repeat offenders may be reprimanded. The ban aimed to address illegal content and platform risks but drew heavy criticism for collateral removals and impacts on communities (e.g., LGBTQ+).

rubrics_metrics.name: November 2022 policy update: allow nudity but not explicit sex
rubrics_metrics.description: In November 2022, Tumblr changed its rules to allow nudity, but not sexually explicit images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represented a partial relaxation compared with the 2018 ban; platform still prohibits explicit sexual content while permitting non-explicit nudity under policy-defined exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic content recognition plus manual review
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr stated it used various algorithms to detect potential violations, in combination with manual reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic classifiers produced wide arrays of false positives; Tumblr committed to reviewing algorithms and appeals processes (including under settlement requirements). Reliance on algorithms carries risk of over-blocking non-violative material.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — mandatory SOGI trainer and training content
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement required the mandatory hiring of a sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) trainer for Tumblr content moderation employees who provides at least 2 hours of interactive cissexism knowledge and avoidance training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training intended to reduce biased moderation against LGBTQ+ content; the trainer must meet qualification-reporting requirements (see related obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — provide trainer name, qualifications, and draft materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the name and qualifications of the SOGI trainer, as well as a draft of their training materials, to the NYCCHR within 90 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required transparency so the regulator can verify the appropriateness of SOGI training content.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — attendance records
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an electronic attendance sheet for the SOGI trainer whose attendance data would be provided to the NYCCHR for 90 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records enable commission monitoring of who received the mandated training.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — proof of completion timing and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proof of completion of SOGI training by the SOGI trainer within 10 calendar days, which could anonymize SOGI trainees in accordance with data protection compliance, including GDPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid reporting of training completion while allowing privacy-protecting anonymization for trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — mandatory training for classifier staff within 120 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Required SOGI training by the SOGI trainer for all Tumblr employees, agents, interns, and independent contractors who work on the adult content classifier, globally, within 120 calendar days following the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both in-house and contracted personnel working on automated adult-content systems to reduce discriminatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — revise appeals form within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Required revision of the adult content appeal form to include text and text entry boxes within 90 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded appeals form fields to capture more context when users contest content removals; part of improving appeals fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — search for SOGI terms in appeal reviews within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Required revision of adult content appeal reviews to include searching for SOGI terms within 60 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly requires evaluators to consider whether SOGI-related terms appear so as to detect and correct biased flagging of LGBTQ+ content.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — manual review sampling and retraining requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Required manual review of 500 appeals from 6 days (for a total of 3,000 flagged posts) randomly selected within 1 day from the past 6 months prior to the settlement to be provided to the NYCCHR for review of SOGI bias, including using a random sample of 500 or 75% (whichever amount was smaller) of the incorrectly flagged images and subsequent successful appeals to retrain the adult content classifier on a monthly basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a concrete auditing and retraining cadence using misclassification samples to reduce classifier bias on an ongoing monthly schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — reporting requirements for SOGI-related appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Required reporting of the number of SOGI-related appeals from the first business day of the second month following the settlement and continuing for the next 18 months to the NYCCHR, including monthly reports of the monthly number and percentage (of the whole of appeals) of SOGI-related appeals, plus the same information from the prior month, within 10 business days of the first business day of each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates detailed monthly transparency about appeals volume and SOGI-related share to enable regulator oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — process to seek exemption for infeasible steps
rubrics_metrics.description: An allocation for Tumblr to request being absolved from any infeasible steps of the prior list with NYCCHR approval, which would require a detailed description of why it was infeasible, including economic records if the reason presented were economic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a formal process for Tumblr to seek relief from operationally infeasible obligations subject to regulator review and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — expert classifier review report within 180 days
rubrics_metrics.description: A required review report of the classifier expert's analysis of the adult content classifier's SOGI bias, steps taken to correct the bias, and ultimate evaluation of the adult content classifier and SOGI discrimination written in plain English and submitted to the NYCCHR within 180 calendar days of the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires an expert audit and public-facing plain-English summary of corrective actions and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — public posting of obligations and notice posters
rubrics_metrics.description: Required public posting of new company obligations under the settlement in the employee notice area in compliance with NYC Human Rights Law, alongside the commission's Notice of Rights and LGBTQ Rights posters in both English and Spanish within 30 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures employees are informed of new obligations and rights in accessible languages and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCCHR settlement — staffing allocation for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A required assignment of 9 Tumblr employees to assist with settlement processes and reviews as needed for at least 6 months following the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates dedicated personnel capacity to implement and monitor settlement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMCA takedown compliance and risk of weaponization
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr accepts Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) takedown notices; the site has been criticized for copyright infringements by participating bloggers and for being weaponized by actors filing DMCA notices to disrupt or delist content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform responds to valid DMCA notices; stakeholders should be aware of both legitimate takedown process and potential misuse to suppress content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reblog editing restrictions (2015 change)
rubrics_metrics.description: In July 2015, the reblogging system was modified so that users cannot remove or edit individual comments by other users when reblogging a post; existing comments can only be removed all at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to combat 'misattribution' but was criticized by ask and roleplay (RP) communities that used comment editing to improve readability and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reblog display format change (2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: In September 2015, threads of comments on reblogged posts were changed from a nested view with indentations to a flat view; user avatars were also added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to improve legibility especially on mobile, but some users felt it reduced the site's nostalgic charm; policy/UX changes can trade readability vs community aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ephemeral group chats feature (2019–2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group chats were ephemeral chat rooms surfaced via searches that allowed users to share content in real-time; posts disappeared after 24 hours and could not be edited. The group chat function was discontinued on September 22, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature trial and subsequent discontinuation demonstrates product experimentation and removal based on usage/fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post+ monetization rollout and removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr launched Post+ (a blogger monetization feature) on July 21, 2021 for some beta users; Post+ was removed in January 2024 due to low usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization features may be trialed and later removed if adoption is low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip feature removal
rubrics_metrics.description: A tipping feature introduced in February 2022 was removed on June 1, 2024 due to low usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization or micro-payment features can be deprecated if not broadly adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestreaming product lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr announced a livestreaming service called Tumblr Live at end of 2022, adapted from a third-party product; Tumblr announced discontinuation of Tumblr Live in 2024 with migration options for users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party integrations and rebranded features may be temporary and include migration support when discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising, promoted posts, and ad-free subscription
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr monetized via advertising (promoted posts, brand campaigns). In July 2016 advertisements were implemented by default across all blogs (users may opt-out). In February 2022 Tumblr launched an ad-free subscription option for $5/month or $40/year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform monetization strategies include default ads, promoted content, and paid ad-free subscriptions; changes to ad policies can affect user experience and revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-level access blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Several countries have blocked access to Tumblr because of pornography, religious extremism or LGBTQ content (examples: China, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Iran).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform content policies and local laws can lead to national-level blocking or pressure to self-censor; operators must consider jurisdictional constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child sexual-abuse material detection and App Store removal (Nov 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tumblr scans images against an industry database; after a routine audit found illegal child pornography on the service, Tumblr's iOS app was removed from the App Store until the issue was addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated scanning against shared industry databases is used to detect illegal content; discovery of such content can lead to app-store enforcement and wide product consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search results safety for self-harm queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching terms like 'depression', 'anxiety', and 'suicide' on Tumblr brings up a PSA page directing the user to resources (e.g., National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, The Trevor Project) and offers an option to continue to search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform safety features surface support resources proactively for queries that indicate self-harm risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifier retraining using misclassification samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Under settlement commitments, Tumblr must use a random sample of incorrectly flagged images and successful appeals to retrain the adult content classifier on a monthly basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalizes continuous improvement of automated moderation by retraining on verified misclassifications to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy exceptions for illustrations, political/newsworthy nudity, and medical contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit exceptions are provided for illustrations or art that depict nudity, nudity related to 'political or newsworthy speech,' and depictions of 'female-presenting' nipples in relation to medical events such as childbirth, breastfeeding, mastectomy and gender reassignment surgery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation decisions must consider context (art, newsworthy, medical) and not treat all nudity identically; documentation of exceptions is necessary for consistent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tags as commentary vs descriptive metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Two main tag uses on Tumblr: descriptive tagging (introduced by original poster to describe content for searchability) and tags used as a form of communication (personal, meta-commentary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive tags are important for indexing and discoverability; commentary tags are a community practice to express opinions or background but are not always appropriate for discoverability.
